entities.summary: Ervin Marton was a Franco-Hungarian artist and photographer who became an integral part of the Paris art culture beginning in 1937. An internationally recognized photographer, he is known for his portraits of many key figures in art, literature and the sciences working in Paris, as well as for his candid "street photography". His work was regularly exhibited in Paris during his lifetime, as well as in Budapest, London and Milan. It is held by the Hungarian National Gallery, the Bibliothèque Nationale in Paris, and the Hungarian Museum of Photography, as well as by major corporations and private collectors in Europe and the United States.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent photographer in Paris during World War II, Ervin Marton's work captured images of key figures in art and literature, including artists like Pablo Picasso and writers like Jean Cocteau. His photographs provide valuable insight into the cultural landscape of Paris during this period.
